authoritative_policy.authority: These three fields are the authoritative statement of the policy. Prose in normative documents explains them and cannot change them; the clause registry and lint below keep the prose consistent with them. Provider enforcement covers main only: ruleset 24431688 blocks non-fast-forward updates and deletion of main. Other branches are not provider-protected, and the policy still applies to them.

clauses.list_lead_in: say in the description that a bundle changed.
clauses.text: - **Commit identity.** Maintainer merges and automated commits use a GitHub `noreply` or organization-safe identity; see [docs/PUBLIC_COMMIT_IDENTITY_POLICY.md](docs/PUBLIC_COMMIT_IDENTITY_POLICY.md). Contributors may publish whatever identity they choose.
It can only check the metadata;
Held by the originating project, never published unless separately cleared.

- An administrator can still edit, disable or delete the ruleset. Disabling it, pushing to `main` and enabling it again is possible. That is a configuration change, not a merge through the fence. Nothing here makes privileged ownership incapable of changing provider configuration.
External contributors may sign their own commits with any address they are comfortable making public.
It grants **no** authority to rewrite, filter, rebase or force-push public history.
This policy grants **no** authority to rewrite public history for any reason, including to remove an exposed secret.
- mirroring, transplanting, grafting or filtering private Git history into Commons;
| Non-fast-forward blocked | Force pushes to `main` are not accepted. |

scope: Every normative document: root *.md, docs/*.md and .github/*.md. Reports under reports/ are historical evidence and are not normative.
